expectations.text: Actually connects and inspects multiple collections
expectations.evidence: Response connects to cluster, lists all 12 collections in an inventory table with configs, includes actual metrics from /metrics endpoint showing RSS 25.1 MB, 573 open mmaps. Product-specific details are shown including payload data for products-us and quantization config for embeddings-archive.

expectations.text: Identifies the locale collections antipattern (10+ products-{locale} collections)
expectations.evidence: Issue 5 'Collection proliferation - 10 locale-specific collections with identical schema' identifies the antipattern. Recommends 'Consolidate locale-specific collections into a single products collection with a locale keyword payload field.' Listed as Medium severity.

expectations.text: Identifies products-us issues: vectors in RAM, no quantization, full-text index on description
expectations.evidence: Issue 1 identifies all vectors in RAM (on_disk: false). Issue 2 notes 'Only embeddings-archive has quantization...all 10 products-* locale collections and products-us have quantization_config: null.' Issue 4 discusses 'Bloated payload in products-us' and mentions the text index on description.

Issue 6 'embeddings-archive - quantization configured with always_ram: false but no on_disk vectors' identifies both problems. States 'original 1536-dim float32 vectors are in RAM (200 x 1536 x 4 = 1.17 MB)' and 'int8 quantized vectors are eligible to be on disk.' However, it partially misframes the issue by calling always_ram=false 'correct in intent.'

expectations.text: Provides prioritized recommendations matching Phase 4 order
expectations.evidence: The recommendations are prioritized differently from Phase 4 order. The response orders: 1. consolidate locale collections, 2. enable on_disk for vectors, 3. add quantization to products-us, 4. remove/truncate bloated payloads. The expected Phase 4 order prioritizes fixing embeddings-archive quantization higher than bulk on_disk vector changes. The ordering does not closely match the expected Phase 4 priority table.

expectations.text: Mentions total collection count and overhead calculation
expectations.evidence: The response does not mention the 12-14 MB per-collection overhead or calculate total collection overhead. It discusses WAL capacity (32 MB x 12 = 384 MB) and mmap overhead but never cites the fixed 12-14 MB baseline per collection figure that is central to explaining the memory mismatch.
